messages:
maria: Heads up — I'm proposing a console feature-flag / rollout for toggling a route between JSON/REST and gRPC backends (internal-only). Goal: let clients opt for lower-latency gRPC while preserving a JSON fallback for web SDKs. Need feedback on quotas, telemetry, and rollout UX before I open an RFC.

alex: +1 to the idea. main concern: quota/accounting divergence. gRPC requests tend to batch more and token counting is different. We should avoid double-charging. Suggest a unified "inference_unit" meter emitted at the model-serving boundary rather than at transport layer.

pranav: Agree with alex. Also: add transport metadata to traces/spans: `transport=grpc|rest`, `proto_version=v2` etc. Console panels can then break down latency/cost by transport.

jess: UX notes: the rollout panel needs two knobs: percentage and "error-triggered rollback" (threshold + window). Operators should be able to pin a transport for specific tenants/routes. Visual: stacked area showing percent traffic by transport and error-rate overlay.

li: Architecture note — the gateway should perform transparent fallback, not clients. Flow: try gRPC; on grpc UNAVAILABLE/DEADLINE_EXCEEDED or proto mismatch, gateway rewrites and forwards to REST backend. That centralizes logic and keeps SDKs simple. But gateway must be state-aware to avoid quota mismatch.

maria: li — if gateway rewrites, how do we ensure quota is only counted once? If both gateway and backend emit meters we risk duplication.

alex: We can standardize on emitting the primary meter at the model runtime (where tokens are counted) and have gateway emit only a lightweight 'proxy' metric (requests proxied). Billing uses the runtime meter. Console shows both but only charges the runtime meter.

pranav: For telemetry compatibility: add header `x-transport-hint` when gateway falls back so backend can annotate spans with original transport. That helps diffs in console. Also capture `proto_version` in log context for schema-evolution tracking.

jess: UX: Add a "protocol toggle" audit trail in the rollout UI (who clicked, when, previous %). Also a quick link to open the diff of proto schemas involved. :eyes:

li: Gateway config sketch (pseudo YAML):
```
routes:
  - name: inference-v1
    backend_candidates: [grpc://model-a, http://model-a-json]
    policy: prefer=grpc, fallback=rest
    fallback_reasons: [UNAVAILABLE, PROTO_MISMATCH]
    emit_headers: [x-transport-hint]
```
This keeps policy explicit.

maria: Nice. On quotas: do we want per-route quotas or continue tenant-global? I worry per-route could be gamed with many routes.

alex: Keep global tenant quotas as the single source of truth. Expose per-route soft quotas in console for visibility and local throttling, but enforcement happens at runtime. That way tenants can't bypass limits by adding routes.

pranav: Implementation detail: telemetry pipeline needs a join key — `tenant_id + route + transport + proto_version` so the dashboards can slice any axis. Make sure schema doesn't explode (use sampling tags for high-cardinality proto fields).

jess: For rollout UX, propose a "canary script" that ramps 0 -> 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with hold conditions: p95 latency delta < 15% AND error rate < 0.5% absolute. Allow manual override.

li: Edge case: browser clients that only support JSON — gateway must not strip CORS or break streaming behavior when falling back. Keep streaming toggles separate.

maria: Good callouts. I'll draft an RFC with: gateway policy schema, telemetry header conventions, unified meter at runtime, console rollout UI mockups, and recommended canary script. Will assign owners.

deploy-bot: Scheduled canary job created: `protocol-toggle-canary/inference-v1` starting 2024-04-03T16:00Z.

ops-bot: Alert rule added: `TransportErrorSpike` — fires if transport error rate increases by >5% over baseline in 5m. Channels: #incidents, #eng-platform.

alex: small addendum — add an integration test that simulates proto-mismatch fallback so we don't regress.

maria: Thanks all — I'll post the RFC draft in #eng-platform tomorrow and tag owners. :rocket:
